DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The clinical picture of a newborn with dark, "tea-colored" urine and "pea-soup" smelling stool strongly suggests severe salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia, leading to dehydration and potential adrenal crisis. We have ruled out infectious, metabolic (amino acid), and respiratory causes through our extensive workup. Immediate genetic testing and hormone levels are required to confirm.
